name: raid
protocol: Per-domain thresholds set on human texts to 5% FPR, then TPR on machine texts; also 1% FPR and AUROC. Scored only by submitting predictions to the RAID leaderboard (pull request to liamdugan/raid), with and without adversarial attacks.
notes: Test labels and strata are hidden; the split holds only id and generation. 11 LLMs, 11 genres, 4 decoding strategies and 12 adversarial attacks per the Hub card (arXiv 2405.07940). The GenAI Detection Task 3 at COLING 2025 used this split.

name: raid_extra
protocol: As RAID, computed locally since labels are public; the RAID paper reports it in Table 7 (code, Czech news, German news).
notes: Not an official test split, held out because it is our only RAID evaluation with labels. Python code, Czech and German news. RAID's train split trained some detectors (e5-small-lora and SuperAnnotate per their cards), so RAID numbers of those detectors are in-distribution. Its code rows (386,400) are trained on as the source raid_extra_code, so the benchmark is the Czech and German news rows (825,300 and 827,400): unseen domains and languages, generators and attacks of RAID train.

name: mage
protocol: AvgRec, the mean of human and machine recall at the detector's threshold, and AUROC (MAGE paper, Table 3).
notes: The repo loads through a script, which the datasets library no longer runs, so the loader reads test.csv itself; datasets-server's default test split (60,743 rows) is presumably this file. label 0 is machine and 1 is human (GitHub README). src holds '<domain>_<human|machine>_<prompt>_<model>'. 27 generators and 10 human sources per the README; which paper testbed this split is was not verified.

name: mage_ood
protocol: MAGE Testbed 7, unseen domains and unseen model (GPT-4); AvgRec and AUROC (paper Table 11).
notes: Loaded from the file with data_files, so the datasets library names its one split 'train'. 800 machine and 762 human rows, counted here.

name: mage_ood_paraphrase
protocol: MAGE Testbed 8, sentence-level gpt-3.5-turbo paraphrase of Testbed 7; AvgRec and AUROC (paper Table 11).
notes: The benchmark labels paraphrased human text (src '*_human_para') as machine; Litmus reads it as ai under this map, and a mixed reading is a choice to report beside it. 1,600 machine and 762 human rows, counted here.

name: semeval2024_task8_a_mono
protocol: Accuracy of hard labels on the gold test set (task overview, arXiv 2404.14183, Table 9).
notes: An unofficial Hub mirror of the organizers' release. 16,272 human and 18,000 machine rows (datasets-server statistics). The data is M4GT-Bench Task 1 (arXiv 2402.11175), so M4GT-Bench has no separate row.

name: semeval2024_task8_a_multi
protocol: Accuracy of hard labels on the gold test set (task overview, Table 10).
notes: Unofficial Hub mirror. Languages were not recounted here; the overview lists them (Table 2).

name: hc3
protocol: No official test split or metric; report AUROC and TPR at fixed FPR on all answers.
notes: 24,322 questions, each with lists of human and ChatGPT answers; the loader explodes both lists. The repo loads through a script, so the loader reads all.jsonl, the union of the five domain files. ChatGPT (Dec 2022) only.

name: beemo
protocol: AUROC per pair of text versions: H vs M, E vs M, H vs E, L vs M, H vs L, G vs M, H vs G (paper Table 4). The paper's main task counts expert-edited text as machine.
notes: Evaluation-only benchmark (one split named train). 2,187 prompts and 10 instruction models; LLM edits are stored as a list of three prompt variants (P1 to P3), which the loader explodes. Expert-edited machine text maps to Litmus's mixed origin.

name: mixset
protocol: Binary MGT vs HWT as the benchmark labels it (LLM-as-a-Coauthor, arXiv 2401.05952). Every text is mixed in Litmus's sense; report the mixed reading beside it.
notes: 500 MGT and 100 HWT rows; 12 mixing operations of 50 rows each (datasets-server statistics).

name: apt_eval
protocol: Share of AI-polished human texts flagged as AI at the detector's threshold, by polishing degree and share polished (ACL Findings 2025; arXiv 2502.15666, Table 6 thresholds).
notes: Every row is human text polished by one of 5 LLMs (degree-based and percentage-based). The card's table totals 15,004 including 300 pure human texts; datasets-server reports 14,650 rows for the repo's default test split, presumably this file; not recounted.

name: apt_eval_human
protocol: The unpolished human originals of APT-Eval, scored for the false positive baseline.
notes: 300 rows per the dataset card ('no-polish / pure HWT'); not recounted.

name: editlens
protocol: Ternary human, AI-edited, AI-generated accuracy and macro F1 with thresholds from the validation split (EditLens, arXiv 2510.03154, Tables 1 and 2).
notes: Gated: accept the terms on the Hub before loading. Columns were not visible to this check, so text and label columns are blank and the loader refuses the row until they are set. Also data/test_enron and data/test_llama files (splits test_enron and test_llama). Columns read on 2026-11-18 with the forwarded token: text, text_type, model, source, source_id, source_text, split.

name: codet_m4
protocol: Binary macro F1 and accuracy on the test rows (CoDet-M4, arXiv 2503.13733, Table 2).
notes: The Hub stores one split; the 'split' column marks 405,069 train, 47,734 val and 47,749 test rows, so the loader filters to test. Holding out by (repo, config, split) holds out the whole repo.

name: droid
protocol: Binary and ternary F1 as in the DroidCollection paper; the paper was not read here.
notes: Test: 49,932 human, 26,524 machine, 16,140 adversarial machine, 13,230 machine-refined (datasets-server statistics). In distribution: the first corpus trains on its train and dev splits (`droid_collection` in corpus/sources.csv), so it is not an unseen family.

name: autextification_en
protocol: Subtask 1 (IberLEF 2023) macro F1 of hard labels on the test set.
notes: 10,642 human and 11,190 generated rows per the card. Generators are anonymized letters A to F (BLOOM and GPT-3 sizes per the card). Loading script repo; loaded from the TSV with data_files.

name: autextification_es
protocol: Subtask 1 (IberLEF 2023) macro F1 of hard labels on the test set.
notes: 11,209 human and 8,920 generated rows per the card.
